ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the line $I_1 \colon y=x+1$ intersects with the line $I_2 \colon y=mx+n$ at point $P(a, 2)$. What is the solution set of the inequality $x+1\ge mx+n$ in terms of $x$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $y=x+1$ intersects with the line $I_2 \colon y=mx+n$ at point $P(1, 2)$,\\
substituting $y=2$ into $y=x+1$ gives $x=1$,\\
therefore, the coordinates of point $P$ are $(1, 2)$;\\
From the graph, it is known that when $x \geq 1$, $x+1 \geq mx+n$.\\
Thus, the answer is: $\boxed{x \geq 1}$.
